UK inflation rose in March in a clear sign of the impact of the Iran-US war on the economy.

The latest figures, released on Wednesday, are the first from the Office for National Statistics to include elevated petrol and diesel costs since the start of the conflict. Prices have gone up as a result of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz shipping corridor.

The ONS figures showed Consumer Prices Index (CPI) inflation rose 3.3 per cent in the year to March, up from 3 per cent in February.

The increase marks a blow for chancellor Rachel Reeves, who made cutting the cost of living her number one priority. Research by the Resolution Foundation has found the average household will be £480 worse off this year due to increased energy costs.

In response, Ms Reeves said the Iran crisis was “not our war, but it is pushing up bills for families and businesses”.

Chancellor Rachel Reeves said the Iran crisis was 'not our war, but it is pushing up bills for families and businesses' ( PA )

She continued: “That’s why it’s my number one priority to keep costs down.

“Our economic plan is the right one and has put us in a stronger position to support families in the face of this new crisis.”

Pointing to measures announced before the conflict, she said: “We’ve taken £117 off energy bills, frozen rail fares and protected motorists with the fuel duty freeze.

“We’re acting to protect people from unfair price rises if they occur to bring down food prices at the till, and are boosting long-term energy security — building a stronger, more secure economy.”

Heating oil, some food prices including chocolate and fish, and airfares all contributed to the rising prices, with Sanjay Raja, chief UK economist at Deutsche Bank, noting that the former was one of the first commodities to show the impact of the war.

“Energy prices rose substantially with pump prices up just under 8 per cent month-on-month and heating oil prices up a staggering 90 per cent,” he said.

“Food prices were a little stronger than we thought - both processed and unprocessed with foods and yoghurt, chocolate, fish all seeing bigger gains than we expected. Services prices also shot up – but only because of airfares, which jumped 10 per cent. Core goods inflation remained subdued on the back of weaker clothing prices, furniture prices, car prices, and IT goods such as software.

“The good news – if any – was that our core services measures, which strip out some of the more volatile elements in the services basket remained broadly unchanged. And near-term CPI is still expected to take a big step down as base effects drag on the annual rate. The bad news? The drop won’t be as big as we previously anticipated.”

The rise in inflation also means the Bank of England is unlikely to cut interest rates any time soon. Before the Iran war, it had signalled that it might cut rates two or three times this year from the present 3.75 per cent - though unemployment figures falling in Tuesday’s data at least eases the BoE’s two-way tug-of-war in that regard, as rising unemployment is another reason to cut rates, while inflation is an argument to hike them.

Dropping rates would have led to cheaper new mortgages and lower borrowing costs for businesses.

“Inflation is likely to remain elevated in April too, and markets are now pricing in one rate rise later this year, but our house view is that rates are held through the conflict – returning to the expected rate cutting cycle later than forecast just a couple of months ago, but on path to neutral next year,” explained Emma Wall, chief investment strategist at Hargreaves Lansdown, while Samuel Fuller, director of Financial Markets Online, warned it was “premature to dismiss the UK's inflationary threat”.

“This March data only captures the inflationary impact of the first month’s fighting, and April’s data may prove much worse,” he added.

The news on inflation comes amid fears that a further escalation in the Middle East conflict could also impact government borrowing.

The influential Resolution Foundation has found that a “severe but plausible scenario”, in which the conflict intensifies and delivers the largest hits to the economy, would result in government borrowing increasing by £16 billion a year in 2029-2030.

RAC data from 16 April showed that the average price of a litre of petrol at UK forecourts was 158.1p, 25p more expensive than when the war began on 28 February.

The average price of a litre of diesel sits at 191.2p, up 49p compared with the start of the war.

Economists at Oxford Economics said they expect the rise in pump prices to add between 0.2 and 0.3 percentage points to the rate of inflation in March.

News.title: Britain launches new mRNA vaccine trial to prepare for bird flu pandemic
News.content:
A major new clinical trial for an mRNA bird flu vaccine is set to begin in Britain in the coming weeks, it was announced on Wednesday.

The trial will recruit 3,000 participants from across the country to assess how effectively the jab protects against the virus which scientists fear could trigger the next pandemic.

The study is being led by Moderna in partnership with the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the government body responsible for managing threats to public health in Britain.

Originating in birds, the H5N1 virus has spread rapidly through animal populations in recent years, decimating millions of farmed birds worldwide and infecting a range of mammals, including dairy cattle, cats, bears and foxes.

Since 2024, at least 114 human cases have been recorded, all linked to close contact with infected animals.

The new vaccine uses messenger RNA technology – the same platform that enabled the rapid development of several Covid-19 vaccines.

It allows for faster production than traditional methods and is considered particularly suited to responding quickly during large-scale outbreaks.

“By advancing research on an investigational mRNA vaccine against pandemic influenza and supporting rapid clinical trial delivery in the UK, we are helping build the evidence, experience and readiness that can inform future responses to emerging public health threats,” said Darius Hughes, UK General Manager at Moderna.

News.title: Liam Rosenior turns on Chelsea players after ‘unacceptable’ performance
News.content:
Rosenior said any players who cannot handle the pressure and criticism that comes with representing Chelsea should not be at the club. He added that he understands the frustrations of the supporters who targeted him personally during the game.

“It’s my job as the head coach and the manager of the football club,” Rosenior said. “The buck stops with me. I have thick skin and I understand why the fans are frustrated. I’m frustrated with the performances we are putting in.

“What I need to do is look at how we go about games, the personnel of the team, who I can trust and rely on in difficult moments, because not enough players showed that today in the game.

“It’s not about playing for me. It’s about playing for the club. It’s about playing for the shirt. It’s about playing to win games of football. I can speak on what I saw tonight. You can read anything into it that you want, whether they’re playing for me or not, but that performance in itself was damning. It stood against everything that I believe in.

“I have always said I will be honest, and I’ve been honest with the players. I’m honest with you [the media], as honest as I can be. I’m not throwing anyone under the bus. That was an unacceptable performance. And I’m at the head of that.

“I’m managing Chelsea – criticism and pressure comes with the football club. So if you can’t handle that, then you shouldn’t be here. It’s as simple as that. And that’s something that needs to be addressed this week. But it also needs to be addressed in the long term.”

Trevoh Chalobah, the Chelsea defender, added: “We can be accountable. As players we have to be accountable for the performance. We know how much the fans have been behind us and we know they are disappointed with the results, not winning at the moment. We just have to stick together and pull through.

“I thought personally that the boys were running their socks off. Everyone in the changing room is tired. It’s nothing to do with effort. We gave it our all, we just got beat today.

“We have to stay positive. Negativity is not going to help. Us being negative, us dwelling on the past is not going to help the situation so we have to. No matter what happens in life you have to keep going forward and pick ourselves up.”

Chelsea fans target Rosenior as club lurch into deeper crisis

News.title: O’Sullivan plots path to Higgins after pushing World Snooker Championship debutant to the brink
News.content:
Ronnie O’Sullivan has taken a giant step towards a mouth-watering second round match against fellow 50-year-old John Higgins with a highly impressive start to his quest for an eighth world snooker title.

Despite initially heading for the wrong table on his return to the Crucible, O’Sullivan looked instantly back at home following a mixed season spent largely outside of England that has contained recent hints of a return to form.

O’Sullivan raced to a 5-0 lead before sharing the final four frames of the opening session of his first round match against China’s He Guoqiang to lead 7-2 ahead of the conclusion on Wednesday afternoon.

Although O’Sullivan did reach the semi-final last year, he looked bereft of confidence with what was a new cue before being comprehensively outplayed by the eventual winner Zhao Xintong.

Despite another year and a few more grey hairs, it was instantly obvious that O’Sullivan arrives in Sheffield this year rather happier with both his form and chances of moving clear of Stephen Hendry to become the only eight-times world champion in the modern era.

It helped that Guoqiang missed a series of early chances in what was a wide-open match, but O’Sullivan’s usual break-building fluency was crucially also matched by some well struck long pots and clearances when the balls were not always invitingly placed.

The early burst of frames included breaks of 72, 97 and 113 before Guoqiang’s brief fightback was halted by further runs of 52 and 86.

Should O’Sullivan complete the expected victory, the second round will be a rerun of the final against Higgins exactly 25 years ago, which he won 18-14 to win his first world title.

Higgins and Mark Williams, the third 50-plus member of the Class ‘92, are respectively going for their fifth and fourth world title.

Although O’Sullivan has now slipped furthest down the rankings, that is largely explained by his much more limited tournament schedule. There have been encouraging signs in recent months, however, with O’Sullivan following up his 153 total clearance in the International Open in China with a resounding victory against Higgins in the final of the invitational John Virgo Trophy in Ireland last week.

News.title: Wage growth slumps to five-year low
News.content:
Workers are seeing the slowest pay rises in more than five years in a blow to households already facing soaring bills triggered by the war in Iran.

Average wages grew by 3.6pc in the three months to February, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). This was the weakest rise since the quarter to November 2020.

Adjusting for inflation, British workers’ pay increased by only 0.2pc.

Slowing wages will raise the pressure on families, as the war in Iran pushes up the cost of living.

The ongoing conflict is expected to drive up food inflation to more than 9pc by the end of the year, according to forecasts by the Food and Drink Federation. Average households energy bills are expected to rise close to £2,000 a year, while petrol and diesel prices have already spiked.

Martin Beck, chief economist at WPI Strategy, said: “Weaker pay growth will compound the squeeze on households from higher energy prices and supply chain disruption linked to the conflict in the Middle East.

“While recent diplomatic developments may limit the worst-case outcomes, a period of falling real wages is still likely in the second half of the year, weighing on consumer spending and, in turn, labour demand.”

The public sector is better protected, with wages still growing by 5.2pc annually compared with a rise of 3.2pc in the private sector.

Unemployment surprisingly fell before the conflict, the ONS said, though it remains the hardest time since Covid to find a job with far more jobseekers than open roles.

The jobless rate fell to 4.9pc in December to February, down from 5.1pc in the previous three months.

Economists said the fall was mainly driven by rising economic inactivity, meaning they are no longer classified as unemployed, rather than more people finding work.

Modupe Adegbembo at Jefferies said: “This apparent improvement was entirely flattered by falling participation rather than stronger hiring. The decline in labour force participation mechanically reduced the unemployment rate, masking continued softness in actual labour demand.”

The number of employees on the nation’s payroll fell by 65,000 in the year to March.

Job losses have been concentrated among younger workers, with 242,000 fewer people under the age of 35 in work since since Rachel Reeves’s maiden Budget in October 2024, ONS figures show. By contrast, there are almost 100,000 more people aged 35 and older employed compared to October 2024.

There are now 2.5 unemployed people per vacancy, which makes it is the toughest time to find work since early 2021.

The number of advertised jobs fell to 711,000 in March, the lowest number in five years. Outside of the pandemic, vacancies are at an 11-year low.

News.title: West Ham earn point to confirm Wolves relegation and increase Spurs fears
News.content:
West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen, asked if it was a point won or two dropped, said: “It’s probably a bit of both. We did have some chances that on another day could go in but I don’t think a point here is the worst thing in the world.”

West Ham host Everton on Saturday, with Spurs travelling to Wolves, whose relegation was confirmed by the draw at Selhurst Park. Second bottom Burnley will join them in the Championship if they lose to Manchester City on Wednesday.

Nuno managed Wolves from 2017 to 2021, leading them from the Championship to the Europa League quarter-finals. “I feel for them,” he said. “They are a giant club and I’m sure that they can get back.”

The Portuguese was sacked by Nottingham Forest in September last year and was appointed as Graham Potter’s successor at West Ham the same month. Forest, also in the relegation equation and now managed by another former Wolves head coach in Vitor Pereira, are three points ahead of West Ham in 16th place.

Palace manager Oliver Glasner, whose side are 10 points ahead of West Ham in 13th, had raised eyebrows last week by allowing his players to party with fans in Florence after beating Fiorentina on aggregate to reach the European Conference League semi-finals.

Sports.title: Man Utd star opens up on whirlwind 24 hours after shock bench spot vs Chelsea and being compared to David Beckham
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED starlet Jim Thwaites received a shock call-up to the first-team bench just 22 hours after a gruelling Youth Cup shift.

Fresh off a 120-minute marathon in the semi-final, the 18-year-old midfielder capped a whirlwind week by joining Michael Carrick’s senior squad.





The final whistle had barely blown on the Under-18s’ 2-1 win over Crystal Palace before Thwaites was dialling his parents with the life-changing news.

First-team coach Travis Binnion told the Cumbrian kid he would be heading to Stamford Bridge the following morning for the 8pm Premier League kick-off.

Speaking in his first sit-down with the Manchester press pack, Thwaites said: “I was delighted.”

“Obviously on Friday night I was concentrating on the game and getting the job done there, which we managed to do as a team.

“And then after the game, I was told I was on the bench for the first-team on against Chelsea, so I was over the moon.”

Thwaites has already come back down to earth as he prepares to face Palace again in the U18 Premier League Cup final at Selhurst Park tonight.

The midfielder was added to Carrick’s bench as a late replacement after Leny Yoro suffered a hip injury following the defeat to Leeds.

“Take in all the knowledge from them, so I really enjoyed it.”

The youngster an unused sub as United beat Chelsea 1-0, boosting their Champions League qualification hopes after two seasons out of the Europe‘s elite competition.



Thwaites has been called a ‘cheat code’ for his set-piece specialism and ability to play to a high level across midfield.

A stunning free-kick in the U18s’ derby win against City in February earned the youngster comparisons to United icon David Beckham.

On being compared to Becks, Thwaites said: “Well, it wouldn’t be bad to be like him, would it?

“But no, I’ve obviously seen stuff on social media, but I just try and stay grounded about it and focus on my own performances before looking at all that sort of stuff online.

“So yeah, obviously not a bad comparison, though!”



Thwaites, who was called up to train under former United managers Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, signed his first pro deal in December 2024.

He returned to Darren Fletcher’s U18 squad after a lengthy injury lay-off to face City and will travel to the Etihad for the FA Youth Cup final before May 9.

He is knocking on the first team door ahead of next season and a summer window where United are looking to sign two midfielders.

The youngster said: “Well you only have to look at Arsenal and the way they do it, like, they are massive from set pieces.



“So if I try and take that to another level, then it’s only gonna help me in the future when I go and play for different teams or playing the first-team for United, whichever level I get to, it’s only gonna benefit me.”

Thwaites is not the only academy star earning comparisons.

Armer, who also trained with the first team under Ruben Amorim, has seen the viral comments comparing his mannerisms to United and England star Harry Maguire.

He said: “Obviously I’ve seen the comparisons to Harry Maguire [laughs]. You can take bits from all of the first-team and the staff.”

Sports.title: ‘He stuck out for me’ – Man Utd wonderkids reveal two most welcoming stars at Old Trafford
Sports.content:
BRUNO FERNANDES and Lisandro Martinez stand out as the most welcoming stars at Manchester United.

That is the view of academy midfielder Jim Thwaites and youth defender Dan Armer who have trained with the first-team this season.





Thwaites and Armer sat down for their first interview ahead of the Under-18s Premier League Cup final against Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park on Wednesday.

Armer was called up to senior training for the first time under former head coach Ruben Amorim in October, while Thwaites is even closer to breaking into the senior midfield.

Discussing which players made him feel most at home, Thwaites said: “All of them are really good to be fair.

“The ones that stand out for me are Bruno and Martinez. They are really good.

“They are the main two I would say, but as a whole they are all really good with the lads.

Armer said: “Yes, I’d agree. I’d say that Bruno is very open with the young lads. On the postseason tour last year, I remember he stuck out for me.

Highlighting Fernandes’ leadership qualities, Thwaites added: “Bruno will take you aside on the pitch, have a word with you and make sure you’re alright.



“But also on the pitch he will encourage you and let you know what the standards are.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“The standard you should be aspiring to get to; but also helping you to get to that level. So, it really helps both on and off the pitch.”

Fernandes has stepped up in his captaincy duties this season, with less complaining and more constructive instructions on the pitch.

Armer added: “Yes he will just make a joke with you, trying to help you feel a bit more relaxed around the group.”

Head coach Michael Carrick has made long trips to watch several Under-18 and Under-21 matches since replacing Amorim, but has been a physical presence at their training sessions.



Armer said: “It’s really good to see he’s there because it makes everyone push a little bit more to try and impress. It definitely helps when he comes and watches training.”

Both Thwaites and Armer have played a major role in Darren Fletcher’s U18 side’s path to the FA Youth Cup final against Manchester City.

Both played the full 120 minutes of the semi-final win over Crystal Palace and Thwaites was called to the first-team bench 24 hours later at Chelsea.

United are one win away from extending their record to 12 Youth Cup titles, four years after Kobbie Mainoo and Alejandro Garnacho were crowned champs.



Thwaites, who opened up on his David Beckham comparisons, said: “It inspires you, doesn’t it?

“You only have to look at the last Youth Cup winning side with Kobbie and Garnacho, and look where they are now, both playing in the Premier League.

“So it’s got to inspire you as a young lad to go and achieve what they achieved.”

Armer said: “All the eyes are on the Youth Cup. All the views on the stream, TNT Sports and so everyone knows how big an occasion it is.”



Academy graduate and World Cup hopeful Mainoo has also been a listening ear for midfielder Thwaites, who has played as a No6 and No10 throughout his development.

The teenager said: “He’s a really good lad to talk to, a lad you can learn lots from when you go into the first team sessions.

“So I try to speak to him a bit and adapt my game. [We talk] about how he does well on the pitch. He’s good guy to talk to.”

Thwaites added: “From a young age you get taught to play in numerous positions so for me playing number 6, 8, and 10 is just helping me in the future being able to play all three positions.”

Armer has been working on his diagonal, long-range passing this season and admits he uses U18s games to “try it out more”.

Sports.title: The five dilemmas Man Utd chiefs face over Carrick including Solskjaer factor… and five reasons he should get the job
Sports.content:
THE CHAMPIONS League anthem is all but certain to be restored to the Old Trafford pre-match playlist next season.

That will largely be down to Michael Carrick’s impact since he was parachuted in at Manchester United in mid-January.





Eight wins from 12 games in a sub-standard Premier League season has elevated United to third and sixth-placed Chelsea have been all but cut adrift of the Champions League places.

Two years ago, United pointlessly held an end-of-season review to determine whether or not to sack Erik ten Hag.

After two weeks in which they drew conclusions which had long since been concluded, they lost their nerve and kept Ten Hag as United had won the FA Cup final.

Waiting until this season has concluded to make a decision on Carrick’s position is entirely sensible but United should not require an additional fortnight to make up their minds.

Their final five fixtures could have a bearing. United should be aiming to finish third and coming fourth or fifth would possibly feel anti-climactic.

But, come the final day at Brighton on May 24, there will be ample evidence for United to have decided on whether to stick or twist.

Here are the cases for and against…

The case for…

Results



Since Carrick’s first match in charge – the 2-0 triumph against Manchester City – United have entered the Champions League qualifying places and never dropped out of them.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Such stability has been unheard of at United in the past two-and-a-half years and they have regained a modicum of consistency under their former captain.

Carrick has a win percentage of 67 per cent and overseen victories against top six clubs City, Arsenal, Aston Villa and Chelsea, with potentially a fifth to in the offing against Liverpool next week.

The wins at Arsenal and Chelsea also ended eight-year and six-year droughts at those points of the London compass.



United’s performance level has not matched their results and they peaked in the January derby, their best display since the 2024 FA Cup final.

But results take precedence in the final stretch and United have responded to their two defeats under Carrick with wins.

Even on their worst night under him against Leeds, United were the better side for the final half-an-hour – with ten men.

Ahead of the curve



It is not beyond the realms of possibility that Manchester City, Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea and, or, Newcastle could change coaches in the summer.

For once, uncertainty mounts over the futures of coaches at United’s competitors and United could have a headstart if they keep Carrick.

Come United’s first pre-season friendly against Wrexham on July 18, Carrick would have been back in the building for six months, earned the respect of the players, improved performances, the league position and morale.

The 44-year-old knows what constitutes standards at United and he has assembled an exciting and energetic backroom staff by bringing in Steve Holland and Jonathan Woodgate, whilst retaining the popular Travis Binnion.



Carrick has held dialogue about recruitment and, as a garlanded midfielder, is uniquely placed to advise on how United should go about reinforcing their priority position.

No ideal elite external candidate available

The second favourite for the United job is Julian Nagelsmann, the Germany coach who has not managed in club football for three years.

Behind him are Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner, almost by default as their clubs have already announced they will be leaving in the summer. Then it is Gareth Southgate, more addicted to Linkedin than Liam Rosenior.



This is not like ten years ago, when United had a free run at free agent Jose Mourinho. In 2022, Mauricio Pochettino was going to become available and it cost only £2.5million to release Erik ten Hag from his Ajax contract.

Realistically, it would be an about-turn from United to make a beeline for Xabi Alonso. Xavi has not coached in two years and settling for an exotic name backfired with Ruben Amorim.

Eddie Howe, possibly on his way out at Newcastle, was of greater interest when Dan Ashworth and Sir Dave Brailsford were on the scene at United.

United’s aim is to mount a first genuine title challenge since they last won it next season. Carrick is guaranteed to finish above Premier League peers Iraola, Howe and Glasner, so there is logic in continuing with him.

Academy asset



Carrick has a vested interest in the United academy, given his son Jacey is in it, but his passion is genuine and dates back to his playing days at the club.

His presence at under 18 and under 21 games has given the academy added exposure and Carrick has already coached some members of the FA Youth Cup finalists.

Amorim was not as glowing about the academy’s starlets and most of his criticism was valid.

From the United power brokers’ perspective, having a coach who is invested in the academy ticks a box.



Compliance

Carrick does not rock the boat. Amorim almost caused it to capsize before he effectively engineered his own sacking in the new year.

Some at United would occasionally like Carrick to be more opinionated on particularly positive topics but it is admirable he won’t compromise his placid personality.

Carrick is a collegiate colleague whose press conferences are not cause for the United power brokers to peer through their fingers.



The case against…

Performances

By his own admission, Carrick was dissatisfied with the performance at Chelsea on Saturday.

Since United’s four-game winning streak at the start of Carrick’s tenure ended, their performance level has dipped. United’s most comfortable win – against ten-man Tottenham – required a goal in the final ten minutes to open up a two-goal lead.

Director of football Jason Wilcox’s scrutinising of a lifeless performance against Wolves led to Amorim’s sacking as he took exception to the constructive criticism.



United have not performed as soullessly under Carrick but they have not truly convinced for two months and they need to be confident that Carrick will arrest that.

Busier schedule

Carrick has capitalised on United’s sparse schedule of one game per week but they will have European football next season.

United have had two games under Carrick where they have played three days after their previous fixture and they have won neither of them. Those performances away at West Ham and Newcastle were among their worst.



Even though United’s squad consists of players accustomed to midweek matches, they have nestled into a curious comfort zone of mainly weekend-only games.

Ultimately, Carrick is unproven in juggling a domestic and European schedule, apart from his 11-day caretaker stint in November and December 2021

Better coaches are available

As good a job as Carrick has done, Iraola’s and Glasner’s track records suggest they are better coaches.



Iraola will have completed three seasons with Bournemouth and achieving finishes of 12th, ninth and maybe eighth would be a minor miracle at such a provincial club.

Glasner’s spell at Crystal Palace will total two-and-a-quarter years and he may have packed two trophies into the Eagles’ golden age.

Alonso has a managerial record that trounces Carrick’s, going off his Bundesliga success with Bayer Leverkusen. Perish the thought, but Enzo Maresca and Sean Dyche have achieved more on the touchline.

Some of those names are contrary but there is clear evidence that more experienced managers are on the market.



The Solskjaer factor

It was telling that while Kieran McKenna was attempting to secure a third promotion as Ipswich Town manager and Carrick was attempting to secure the United job at the weekend, Mike Phelan was coaching club legends in South Korea.

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s only job since United sacked him in November 2021 remains his seven-month spell at Besiktas.

It is pretty clear that the innovators from Solskjaer’s United regime were Carrick and McKenna, with Phelan a borderline redundant ‘assistant manager’.



Carrick is a modern coach, unlike Solskjaer, and his mid-season impact seems set to end with Champions League qualification, unlike Solskjaer in 2019.

But the parallels between the old colleagues and friends are still relevant. United got burnt when they upgraded Solskjaer from caretaker to permanent manager and his third and second-placed finishes came during the fake football of the Covid-19 pandemic.

Wilcox, now at United for two years, alarmingly considered rehiring Solskjaer in January. Going for the most in-house external choice could be a slippery slope.

Charisma question

This is a selfish and niche addition but an important one. A United manager usually has to ooze charisma and that is not Carrick’s natural personality.



When the chips were down for Sir Alex Ferguson, he tended to be on his best form in press conferences. Jose Mourinho was similar. Amorim was box office and Louis van Gaal’s wine-and-mince-pie walkout came in the midst of a winless December he somehow survived.

Ferguson said he played two matches a week and one was the press conference. Carrick does not have a game-face on for his weekly gatherings at Carrington and it has not done him any harm so far.

There will be bumps in the road, though, and it is in Carrick’s interests to have some goodwill banked to keep the vultures at bay.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ten Hag came unstuck on that front. Curiously, the Dutchman was a chipper and warm presence off camera but could be cold and gruff on it.



Had he showcased that true personality when the cameras were rolling, Ten Hag might still be in charge of United.

Sports.title: ‘Seriously unserious player’ – Fans can’t believe what Cherki was doing while huge Man City vs Arsenal brawl broke out
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY star Rayan Cherki has caused a stir on social media after fans noticed his latest stunt.

He was spotted doing keepy ups during a huge brawl between City and Arsenal players.





Cherki has built a reputation for being a wind-up merchant following his antics at Wembley after City beat Arsenal in the Carabao Cup final.

He goaded the Arsenal fans while appearing to pretend to be injured.

And fans took to X to react to his latest behaviour as he casually juggled the ball while City and Arsenal players clashed.



One fan posted: “Seriously unserious player.”

Another wrote: “Arsenal fans haven’t seen this footage, they’ll explode.”

While a third said: “Bro just wants to play football.”

City went on to win the huge match 2-1, putting them just three points behind Arsenal with a game in hand.



And Cherki was the star again as he danced through Arsenal’s backline and finished neatly to give his side the lead.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Following Kai Havertz‘s equaliser, top scorer Erling Haaland regained City’s advantage.

The post-match reaction also made headlines as BBC pundits Wayne Rooney and Danny Murphy criticised the City players’ celebrations – branding them “over the top”.

Gianluigi Donnarumma was spotted jumping in the crowd, while Erling Haaland cheekily side-eyed the camera and smirked.



Pep Guardiola has since hit back at the criticism, calling it “stupid“.

Mikel Arteta will be looking to use City’s celebrations as motivation during his side’s title run-in.

Guardiola’s team host Burnley on Wednesday night with a win sending them top of the tree.

They have been at the summit for just six days this whole campaign.

Sports.title: Liam Rosenior turns on ‘indefensible’ Chelsea flops and rages ‘something needs to change’ as job hangs by thread
Sports.content:
LIAM ROSENIOR has sensationally torn into his Chelsea players after their 3-0 away loss to Brighton.

The Blues have now lost five Premier League games in a row and have failed to score in any of those defeats.



They sit seven points adrift of the Champions League places with just four games to play.



When questioned if this was the worst loss of their recent run, under-pressure Rosenior did not hold back.

He said: “By far, by far. That was unacceptable in every aspect of the game. Unacceptable in attitude.

“I keep coming out and defending the players – that’s indefensible.

“That performance tonight, the manner of the goals we conceded, the amount of duels that we lost, the lack of intensity in the team and yeah, something needs to change drastically right now.”



When asked why Chelsea find themselves in this difficult spot, Rosenior let all of his visible frustrations out.

He said: “Why? We need to look in the mirror. I need to look in the mirror. But I can’t keep coming out here and defending some of the things that we’re seeing.

“Manchester United, genuinely result wasn’t there but I felt we turned a corner.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“But the general attitude, spirit was lacking – determination from three or four of the starting eleven. That’s nowhere near enough for this club.



“I can’t come out and lie. I tell the truth. That was an unacceptable performance at every level.”

Chelsea have lost five successive league games without scoring for the first time since November 1912, while their overall five-game losing streak is their longest in the Premier League since November 1993.

They also failed to land a shot on target in a Premier League game for the first time since February 2025, which, coincidentally, was also in a 0-3 defeat against Brighton at the AMEX Stadium.

Rosenior only took over at Stamford Bridge earlier this year, but he made a promising start in the dugout with a string of wins.

All of that equity has quickly faded and now Rosenior is staring the sack in the face.



He does still have an FA Cup semi-final to look forward to at the weekend, but even that might not save his skin come the summer.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Rosenior continued to dissect dismal performance at the Amex Stadium.

He ranted: “The first goal was terrible. We had an easy header and missed the header. The passage before the first goal upset me even more. We had four or five moments to show moral courage, and take the ball down and play. We just kicked the ball back to Brighton.

“You can speak about a lack of confidence, or results not going our way. That doesn’t represent anything that I want to see, and I won’t ever see it again.

“The performance in terms of professionalism wasn’t there. It was a really, really difficult night, the most difficult night – not even here at this magnificent football club – but in my career.



Chelsea player ratings vs Brighton By Lloyd Canfield DISASTER struck Chelsea before the game even kicked off, with Cole Palmer ruled out by a hamstring injury. And things only got worse from there as they were outclassed by Brighton 3-0. Here’s how the players rated… ROBERT SANCHEZ – 5 A visit to his former club could have certainly gone better, and he was given plenty of stick from his old supporters. Made a great save early on to deny Karou Mitoma almost a carbon copy of his goal against Spurs last week, only to concede a minute later after a wicked deflection off of Wesley Fofana. A truly tragic pass out from the back almost had his team 2-0 down within 20 minutes, only for Trevoh Chalobah to bail him out, and his distribution all night was off the pace. He did make several good saves in the game, particularly from Kadioglu in the second half, but was let down significantly by his distribution. MALO GUSTO – 3 Trouble… He was well and truly in it, trying to mark Karou Mitoma. It felt as though the Japanese winger had Gusto’s number from the very start, and the Frenchman wasn’t able to impact the game at all going forward. TREVOH CHALOBAH – 4 Made an utterly vital block on the goal line to bail Chelsea out at 1-0 down after a diabolical pass from Sanchez straight into the path of Carlos Baleba. A lot of the poor defending wasn’t done by him, in fairness, and he was left 2v1 for the Brighton second, but it still wasn’t a strong enough performance to justify being above average. WESLEY FOFANA – 3 The Frenchman had to get a better connection when trying to block Kadioglu’s opener, and mistakenly turned it into his own net. He made plenty of clearances, but was also booked in the first half before being replaced by Alejandro Garnacho. JORREL HATO – 5 It was Hato’s header from Pascal Gross’ corner that fell into the feet of Kadioglu to hit home, which some will say is a bit of bad fortune, and others will say was weak. Actually, despite his error, he’s one of the few Chelsea players who can take some pride in his performance, with some good progression from the back and resilience in his tackling. MARC CUCURELLA – 2 Of all the ex-Brighton players Chelsea have signed, Marc Cucurella takes the biscuit for being the most hated by the Seagulls’ supporters. After leaking the Blues’ team news to his BARBER about Cole Palmer’s injury, he owed the side a good performance, and didn’t pay up. His touch was off, his passing was poor when it mattered, and defensively, he wasn’t good enough either. ROMEO LAVIA – 4 Felt almost invisible in the Chelsea midfield, which is disappointing for a player of his quality. Launched a shot from range over the bar in the first half, and while his passing was good at all distances, it wasn’t progressive enough. MOISES CAICEDO – 1 Caicedo is one of the best midfielders under the sun on his day, but today was not his day, at all. Too often, his passes didn’t work out, he was bullied by Georginio Rutter for Brighton’s second, and then criminally JOGGED back to catch Hinshelwood. His worst game in a Chelsea shirt so far, where he hasn’t been sent off, and against the team that received a pricey £115m for his services, too. ENZO FERNANDEZ – 2 Fernandez returned to being the captain of Chelsea tonight, but it seems that without Reece James fit, there are no role models in this team for the inexperienced players to look up to. He couldn’t get Chelsea ticking going forward, and there seemed to be little in the way of cohesion between midfield and attack at all. PEDRO NETO – 1 The Portuguese winger played a very strange role in this game, almost as a right wing back at times – and he didn’t do it very well. His first touch was poor, his dribbling was often in circles rather than being direct, that was when he wasn’t falling over his own feet. So, so weak on the wing and was relentlessly bullied by Kadioglu physically. LIAM DELAP – 1 Really doesn’t look good enough to play for this club. In all my life, I am not sure I’ve seen a striker look this hapless. He’s physical and strong, but the technical ability is just not there, and Joao Pedro has shown how important it is to have those things blended together. Delap was dealt with easily by Jan Paul Van Hecke, who, to be honest, could’ve been sitting at the back with a glass of wine and a book while defending him. His goalless streak moves up to 21 games. Check out more on Chelsea here.

“Some of the things I witnessed today, I don’t want to ever see again.

“You have to ask the players. If you’re playing at this elite football club, or any football club, to be even accused of throwing the towel in is unacceptable.



“That’s all I’m going to say. I’m hurting, I’m feeling numb. That doesn’t represent me. That doesn’t represent the football club in anyway. That has to change, starting with the FA Cup semi-final on Sunday.”

Given Chelsea’s penchant for changing managers as soon as they fail to challenge, it’s only natural that thoughts are turning to what Rosenior’s future might look like.

The man himself did not want to be drawn into that after such a dissapointing display.

He told reporters: “I don’t want to go into that right now. I have my own thoughts, my own feelings. I have discussed in depth about this football club – regardless of who is the manager – about what needs to happen at this football club for it to be where it needs to be.

“It’s about this football club, Chelsea represents fight, spirit and determination. That was lacking in every department this evening.



“We’ve had injuries. It’s not an excuse, it’s a reality. That team we put out today was far better than its engagement in the game. I will pick a team that will represent the club in the correct manner.

“This was a huge game and we didn’t hit anywhere near the mark. Every game between now and the end of the season is a huge game, and it needs to look like that in the way we play.”

The Chelsea fans chanted “f*** off Rosenior” at thier boss mid-way through the second half as the walls close in on the former Strasbourg man.

When asked about the chants in his post-game press conference, Rosenior did not shy away from criticism.

”I am accountable, I’ve always said that.



“But after tonight, I think the players need to have a look in the mirror for what they put in.

“Tonight was not about tactics. This was about desire, spirit, courage and I did not see enough of that tonight.

“That performance in itself was damning and stood against everything I believe in.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I have thick skin and I understand why the fans are frustrated. I’m frustrated with the performances we’re putting in.

“I am not here to make excuses. That was unacceptable from everyone involved with me at the head of it. That needs to change.”

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola hits back at ‘stupid’ criticism after Wayne Rooney warned antics could come back to bite Man City
Sports.content:
PEP GUARDIOLA has hit back at the “stupid” criticism of Manchester City’s celebrations after beating Arsenal.

BBC pundits Wayne Rooney and Danny Murphy said the full-time whistle scenes at the Etihad on Sunday were “over the top”.





But boss Guardiola said: “People can say whatever stupid things they want — they celebrated because they knew if we didn’t win it would be ‘bye bye’ [for the title]. They won and still we are there. How can they not celebrate it?

“As much as you respect the opponent and their fans, celebrate however you want. We should wait until the end of the season to celebrate? Come on . . . ”

Gianluigi Donnarumma threw himself into the Etihad crowd and skipper Bernardo Silva whipped up fans following the 2-1 victory.

City could have more to toast tomorrow night as a win at Burnley would put them top. Guardiola tells his players to savour victories with fans -often joining them on a post-match walk around the pitch.



He added: “I said to them every game, ‘Go to our supporters’ and enjoy the moment.

“For us it was a final and, of course, you have to celebrate it.”

Pep reckons one reason they were so jubilant was because Arsenal are a “nightmare” to face.

He said: “Seeing how Arsenal play, I give them incredible credit. We had to sweat and fight to win because they have everything.”

Key midfielder Rodri looks set to miss the Clarets clash with a groin injury but the Spaniard is not expected to be out for long.

Meanwhile, Guardiola is tipping his ex-skipper Vincent Kompany to one day replace him at the Etihad.

The 40-year-old Belgian – in charge at Turf Moor the last time City visited almost three years ago – won a second straight Bundesliga title as Bayern Munich boss.



Guardiola said: “Sooner or later, I have a feeling he will decide it is time to come back to England. I’m sure Manchester’s in his heart.

“I said when we played Burnley, ‘He will be a manager here’.”

Sports.title: Paul Pogba on doping ban, what hurt him most and living for the moment at Monaco
Sports.content:
Paul Pogba on doping ban, what hurt him most and living for the moment at Monaco

Former Manchester United and Juventus midfielder Paul Pogba has opened up on the doping ban that saw him suspended from football for 18 months

View 2 Images Paul Pogba is back playing and enjoying his football (Image: 2026 Franco Arland)

Paul Pogba has opened up on his long doping ban - and admits it has changed his perspective towards football and life in general.

‌



Pogba was provisionally suspended after being randomly tested following Juventus' opening game of the 2023-24 season. He later received a four year ban, which was reduced to 18 months in October following an appeal.

‌



Pogba has now resumed his career after signing a deal with Monaco, and appearing on the Rio Ferdinand Presents podcast, the former Manchester United superstar admits he is on a mission to make the most of what remains of his career. Things were so bad for Pogba during his ban that he wasn't even allowed to train with Juventus.

‌



The 32-year-old said: "I'm grateful to be back and play football again, after everything that happened. I see football totally different. I enjoy myself. I want to enjoy it.

"And I want to now arrive at Monaco with a young team. I'm one of the oldest, with the experience to help also the team and also to enjoy myself, you know. What are we going to change? We cannot change. The past is gone. We can only live the moment.

Furious Liam Rosenior points the blame at Chelsea stars as fans turn on manager READ MORE :

Chelsea team news leaked by Marc Cucurella's BARBER hours before Brighton clash READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"And I know I've been out. I've been out for two years. I've been watching the games on TV. I've been staying at Juventus in Italy and I wasn't even allowed to go inside. I was watching the stadium like this every day with my kids telling me, 'Papi, when are you going to go to the game?'

"That, with me, was one of the biggest things. I wasn't allowed to play training matches.

"I was allowed to train (on his own), but I wasn't allowed to play training matches to stay sharp, to be ready for when I came back.

‌



"I wasn't even allowed in training to go there. I had to train in my house or find somewhere to train. Is it normal?"

View 2 Images Paul Pogba is looking to enjoy football again at Monaco (Image: Koji Watanabe/Getty Images)

Pogba admits what hurt him the most was people thinking he was a drug cheat. But he knows the experience has made him stronger.

‌



The World Cup winner added: "I think that's one of the things that got me most. It made me a better, like, more experienced person. A better person also.

"And to be careful, not to trust everybody, you know, and that's it. I mean, this is the way of life. This is part of my story."

Sports.title: Paul Pogba shares one reason for Scott McTominay's success since Man Utd sold him
Sports.content:
Paul Pogba shares one reason for Scott McTominay's success since Man Utd sold him

Paul Pogba spoke to Rio Ferdinand about his former Manchester United teammate Scott McTominay, who has thrived in Italy under Antonio Conte since joining Napoli

View 2 Images Paul Pogba believes Antonio Conte has improved Scott McTominay (Image: Ciancaphoto Studio, Getty Images)

Paul Pogba reckons Napoli boss Antonio Conte is the driving force behind Scott McTominay's impressive performances since departing Manchester United. The Scotland international earned a place in the Serie A's team of the year during his maiden campaign.

‌



Pogba did likewise during his second season with Conte at Juventus. The Frenchman flourished for the Italian in Turin after moving from United in 2012, working together for two seasons and clinching the title in both campaigns before the Italian stepped down.

‌



Conte then secured his fifth Serie A title as a manager, and tenth including his playing days, after bringing in McTominay to Naples last season. The United academy graduate was also named the league's Most Valuable Player.

‌



When quizzed about what has clicked so perfectly for McTominay while appearing on the Rio Ferdinand Presents podcast, Pogba pointed to the former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur manager. "Antonio Conte," he responded.

Paul Pogba on doping ban, what hurt him most and living for the moment at Monaco READ MORE :

"Believe me or not, when I saw that Scott would go to Napoli with Antonio Conte, I said, 'watch. Conte will love him because he has everything that Conte loves.'

"We play, we're teammates. He's a hard worker. Discipline. He trains always like he plays. He's somebody that you know you need to have in your team, that he will give everything, you know, you need someone like that."

‌



Pogba also drew comparisons between McTominay and another Scottish former United midfielder, Darren Fletcher, highlighting the goalscoring prowess of both players.

View 2 Images Antonio Conte and Scott McTominay combined to help Napoli win Serie A last season (Image: Mondadori Portfolio, Mondadori Portfolio via Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"He was kind of like [Darren] Fletcher," Pogba said. "And Scott knows how to score goals. Scott, Fletch [they] knew how to score goals too. Scott scores goals, scores a lot of goals. In training, he always scores, you know.

"And I was like, with Conte, he will make him run, and he likes to run. He's strong. Italian football, they're not too strong. I think it will work. Believe me or not, that's what I said. And I know Conte."

Pogba went on to stress that McTominay's appetite for covering ground and getting about the pitch throughout a match sets him apart in Italy. He added: "Scott loves to run. He loves to, he loves that.

‌



"He has like this character we were talking about. He has this discipline, this thing, this fire inside him. That makes the difference. And with Conte, he can only improve. Conte could only improve Scott, because Scott will know exactly what he will have to do."

Sports.title: 'I was worried we wouldn’t have a football club - now Coventry City are Premier League'
Sports.content:
'I was worried we wouldn’t have a football club - now Coventry City are Premier League'

Coventry City spent 25 years away from the Premier League, and are the first club to ever be relegated from the Premier League to League Two and make their way all the way back up

View 4 Images Frank Lampard celebrates a goal as Coventry batter Portsmouth (Image: 2026 Catherine Ivill - AMA)

Coventry City are a Premier League football team again. And they return as champions.

‌



It feels very surreal writing those words, words I never thought I’d write. Not when suffering relegation to League One and League Two. Not when playing home games at Sixfields, St Andrews or Burton Albion. And definitely not when the club shop was being emptied into the back of a lorry 13 years ago!

‌



To say it’s been a brutally long journey back to the Premier League would be an understatement. It is a journey built on years of suffering, anguish and heartbreak. A club rebuilt and risen from the flames - just like the phoenix in our crest.

‌



The club crest that makes me so incredibly proud to be from Coventry and to support this football club.

WORLD CUP LEGENDS: The stars who lit up football's greatest tournament - Buy the Special Edition today

Frank Lampard makes Coventry transfer plea after sealing Premier League return READ MORE :

Frank Lampard scoops major EFL award after stunning Coventry City promotion READ MORE :

We all know how close we’ve come to the top flight in the last three years. Penalty shootout failure at Wembley and play-off semi-final heartbreak in the final minute last year against Sunderland - agonisingly close.

‌



But last Friday night, in Blackburn, all that pain became worth it. Would promotion feel this good if the agony hadn't been so? I wouldn’t wish it on any club, but it somehow makes the taste of promotion all the more sweeter.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

View 4 Images The Coventry City team celebrate their promotion (Image: Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

‌



I can thank my dad for taking me to my first game, just like his dad took him to his all those years ago. In the old Coventry Telegraph stand, right behind the goal, my introduction to Coventry City were the days of Michael Doyle, Gary McSheffrey, Isaac Osbourne, Elliott Ward, Ben Turner, Claus Jørgensen and Marcus Hall.

The years that followed were full of heartbreak and worry. From worry that we’d keep nosediving down the leagues, to questioning whether there would even be a football club anymore! I was scared that the club which had brought so much joy into my life was going to be non-existent.

Heading down the M1 to Northampton with my dad for our home games was bizarre to say the least, a confusing and difficult time as fans boycotted the games and others watched from Sixfields hill. In the stands, overriding feelings of guilt for being there while still wanting to get behind the boys as others stayed away. A fan base split, a time where it was difficult for both those who went and those who stayed away to support their local team, purely because of how much it had been broken and destroyed.

‌



View 4 Images Coventry City fans protest against the continued ground share at Sixfields in 2014 (Image: Pete Norton)

It just seemed to be a never ending spiral of sending Coventry further down the pyramid and the depths of the football league. On a wintry day in 2013, when the club shop was being emptied into the back of a lorry as we went into administration, that was one of the points I thought it was really over. That we wouldn’t have a football club to support anymore. One moment. A moment that left me devastated and just incredibly sad.

Sometimes all it takes is one moment though. One huge, significant moment to seal the defining point in a season - and Bobby Thomas produced exactly that on Friday night at Ewood Park.

‌



I thought I’d felt euphoria before. Wolves away in the FA Cup quarter final, then again at Wembley against Manchester United in the semi-final before the heartbreaking VAR decision went against us - but this meant much more.

View 4 Images Frank Lampard takes the acclaim after Coventry City sealed promotion (Image: Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

Will Frank Lampard keep Coventry City up next season? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



I celebrated our League One promotion as champions in our back garden with our Covid-bubble, and looking back it is bonkers to think the team were celebrating on top of the Ramada with a DJ set broadcast on YouTube.

This time it’s different. This time we get to celebrate this one properly, a thumping victory over Portsmouth ensuring we get to celebrate together.

Coventry City. Champions. A Premier League club once again.

Sports.title: Man United dream squad for 2026/27 as Anderson signs, Rashford replaced and £44m star joins
Sports.content:
Man United dream squad for 2026/27 as Anderson signs, Rashford replaced and £44m star joins

Manchester United's summer transfer plans could see a major squad overhaul in 2026

View 3 Images Elliot Anderson's arrival would be among the best possible move Manchester United could conduct this summer (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

A wave of change is anticipated at Manchester United this summer, with a decision looming over Michael Carrick's future. And having witnessed a resurgence under the club legend's stewardship, attention now shifts to what business might be conducted in the transfer window.

‌



It's already known Casemiro will be among those departing when his deal runs out at the end of June. However, uncertainty remains over whether club captain Bruno Fernandes will stay following a Player of the Season-worthy campaign.

‌



Marcus Rashford's situation and whether he makes his Barcelona loan permanent will also prove a major talking point in the weeks ahead. Here, Mirror Football examines what other transactions could take place in a dream scenario at Old Trafford.

‌



Anderson rejects Man City

One such priority concerns the requirement for reinforcements in central midfield. To that end, beating Manchester City to the signature of Nottingham Forest's Elliot Anderson would be a coup of the highest order.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

All indications at present point to Anderson being likely bound for City this summer. The player is understood to favour a switch to the Etihad over Old Trafford, even despite the turnaround job Carrick has successfully orchestrated to date.

‌



In an ideal world, however, United would secure the player first and refuse to let go. Even if his reported price tag of £100million or more would account for a substantial portion of the overall funds available this summer.

The likes of Manuel Ugarte and Joshua Zirkzee could be heading out this summer, either of whom could generate some considerable funds to help finance a couple of new arrivals. Signing a player of Anderson's calibre could be a massive boost in any transfer window, but the fact Pep Guardiola's side are seemingly such admirers is just an added bonus.

Rashford replacement

It seems in everyone's best interests if Rashford does ultimately sever ties with his boyhood club this summer, as difficult as that may be to accept. However, Carrick has suggested his former team-mate may still have a future at Old Trafford if he has his way.

‌



Barcelona are still understood to hold an exclusive £26m purchase option on the player, who has experienced a renaissance at the Camp Nou. And while United already have Matheus Cunha excelling predominantly from the left flank this season, additional cover perhaps wouldn't hurt should Rashford leave.

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford looks likely to leave United permanently this summer (Image: AP)

In the interests of preserving squad harmony and ensuring a player like Cunha doesn't grow frustrated, it would be sensible to recruit someone more comfortable operating in a rotational capacity. On that front, a prospect such as RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande could prove a suitable option to vie for a starting berth in attack.

‌



The Ivorian has been in Germany for less than a year since Leipzig activated his £16m release clause. Yet it's testament to just how impressively he's performed in the Bundesliga that his market value is now thought to be closer to the £60m region.

It's understood United are monitoring the forward, though he is also attracting attention from Paris Saint-Germain and other Premier League sides could enter the race. It may prove challenging to prise the left winger away from Leipzig given he remains under contract until 2030.

That said, United should be capable of facilitating negotiations if they demonstrate a willingness to at least meet the 19-year-old's reported valuation.

‌



£44m Stiller signs

View 3 Images Angelo Stiller could be a more cost-effective addition in midfield (Image: Getty Images)

With reports United are prioritising two new midfielders this summer, Stuttgart's Angelo Stiller makes a lot of sense as a lower-profile acquisition. Stiller operates deeper in the midfield chain and would fill the gap set to be left by Casemiro.

That would give the likes of Kobbie Mainoo and Fernandes the freedom to operate more effectively further forward without the risk of leaving Carrick's side vulnerable. The Bayern Munich academy graduate was part of the Stuttgart side that stormed to the DFB-Pokal title last season and is currently on track to help the club secure a place in next term's Champions League.

‌



As it stands, 25-year-old Stiller is understood to have a release clause worth just £32.6m. However, that figure will rise to £43.5m the moment Stuttgart pay a modest fee of around £2m, which appears inevitable at this stage.

Stiller has contributed five assists in the Bundesliga this season, averaging 69.1 passes per game, one of the highest averages for someone who doesn't play in defence.

‌



Final dream 2026/27 squad

Casemiro's departure could ultimately prove to be United's only significant loss this summer, though many will be saddened to see Rashford's time at the club conclude in such disappointing circumstances. As for incoming transfers, the midfield pairing of Anderson and Stiller would bring both quality and depth, while Diomande is displaying all the hallmarks of a future superstar.

Here is how that final squad would look:

Lammens, Bayindir, Onana; Maguire, De Ligt, Martinez, Shaw, Dalot, Yoro, Mazraoui, Heaven, Dorgu; Fernandes, Anderson, Mount, Mainoo, Stiller, Thwaites; Lacey, Cunha, Mbeumo, Sesko, Diomande, Amad, Obi.

Sports.title: 'I'm glad Jurgen Klopp hasn't behaved like Sir Alex Ferguson - he's respected Liverpool'
Sports.content:
Ex-Liverpool striker Michael Owen has praised Jurgen Klopp for keeping his distance from Liverpool since leaving the club in the summer of 2024, contrasting it with the behaviour of former Man United manager Sir Alex Ferguson. While the iconic former United boss has remained a watchful figure at Old Trafford, Owen believes Klopp's decision to largely stay away from Anfield following his departure has been respectful towards his successor Arne Slot.

The England legend's remarks come after the iconic German boss addressed the idea of an Anfield comeback in October last year, claiming it was theoretically possible. The mere presence of a club legend keeping watch over their successors is no doubt a bone of contention with many coaches in world football.

Owen suggested that the near-constant presence of Sir Alex at Old Trafford, since the legendary Scot retired from United in 2013, has affected the string of coaches who've attempted to succeed him since.

Slot won the Premier League title in his first season on Merseyside, but has struggled this year, with many fans calling for his head. However, Klopp has watched on from afar, only returning for a legends charity clash against Borussia Dortmund earlier this month.

‌



Owen, who now represents Casino.org, a leading platform helping players find UK casino brands, exclusively told Mirror Football: "If you look down the East Lancs [road], then, you know, people have had a go at Sir Alex Ferguson for, for 10, 15 years, and basically, Sir Alex says very, very little. He rarely does interviews. He's never, ever, ever been, you know, disparaging or disrespectful to a Manchester United manager.

Michael Owen makes Premier League 1-2-3-4-5-6 prediction with shock inclusion READ MORE :

Fernando Torres backed to 'definitely' become Liverpool boss after Jurgen Klopp offer READ MORE :

"He basically sits in the stand and watches his old team. Now, Jurgen Klopp doesn't do that. He doesn't come back and sit in the director's box and look down on the manager. The role that he's in, at Red Bull, he is thrown in front of journalists an awful lot.

"You know, he is getting asked these questions, and I'm pretty sure that if he didn't have to do the press, he wouldn't be out on X, and writing out statements about the state of Liverpool.

View 3 Images Jurgen Klopp has made feelings clear on a potential return to club management (Image: PETER POWELL, AFP via Getty Images)

‌



"I don't think he wants to do that. But obviously, it's probably part of his job to do the press sometimes and people ask him. So, no, I think in the main, Jurgen Klopp has been very respectful towards the Liverpool manager. He was keen to back Slot and he even started the song at Anfield, didn't he?"

Despite Slot earning breathing room thanks to Liverpool's stunning late win on Sunday against local rivals Everton, the pressure on the Dutchman remains. Owen, who scored 158 goals in eight seasons at Anfield, says Klopp could return to the Liverpool dugout, should Slot leave the club this summer.

However, he clarified that such a turn of events is perhaps more of a fantasy than anything else, citing Klopp's initial reason for stepping down: that the German was running out of the energy required to steer a Premier League and Champions League-chasing club.

"I would say it's wishful thinking, but you'd never know, do you? You absolutely never know," Owen said. "They say never go back. It was just such an amazing, brilliant and beautiful dream of a period for Liverpool, with Jurgen Klopp in charge.

‌



View 3 Images Sir Alex Ferguson has been spotted watching Manchester United on countless occasions since stepping down as manager in 2013 (Image: PA Wire)

"Some of the happiest moments of a lot of Liverpool fans' lives will be the Klopp era. So, I'm sure that lots of Liverpool fans would dream of that scenario. "And I guess if he's going to click his fingers and [Klopp] said, 'Right, I want to come back', then Liverpool would have a big decision to make because it's not like the current management are pulling up trees. Once it's in your blood, it's hard to get out, isn't it? That's the thing.

"So I do see it in many ways. I do see Jurgen Klopp potentially wanting to come back to management, but he did manage Liverpool for a long, long time and obviously decided, 'Right, time's up' - whether he'd want to go and do it again [I don't know]. Because you need some energy to go and pick it all up again and start again from afresh. It would be fascinating, but I would say more wishful thinking rather than reality."

Sports.title: How Liverpool could line up under Fernando Torres as he's backed to 'definitely' be new boss
Sports.content:
How Liverpool could line up under Fernando Torres as he's backed to 'definitely' be new boss

Former Liverpool star Fernando Torres has been backed to take charge of his old club in the future

View 2 Images Fernando Torres has impressed as a coach at Atletico Madrid (Image: ANP, ANP via Getty Images)

Fernando Torres has been tipped as a future Liverpool manager following his impressive work as a coach at Atletico Madrid. The 42-year-old enjoyed a hugely successful stint with the Reds during his playing career and has been backed to make a return to Anfield in a different capacity.

‌



Liverpool have struggled through a difficult second campaign under Arne Slot, with the reigning Premier League champions now focusing on securing Champions League qualification. While the manager has faced criticism this season, the club are not expected to sack Slot, whose contract runs until 2027.

‌



Torres retired from playing in 2019 and took up a coaching role with Atletico's U19 side two years later. He briefly shadowed Jurgen Klopp during the German's final year at the Reds, several months before taking charge of Atletico B. Torres' former Spain team-mate Fernando Llorente has argued it is a question of when, not if, he lands the Liverpool job.

‌



"Fernando Torres as Liverpool manager one day? Definitely," he told Hajper. "He's taken a different path to [Como manager] Cesc Fabregas, he has been patient and has preferred to start little by little with the youth team, gaining experience.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"I think Fernando will become a great coach because he had an incredible career, knows a lot about football and has surely been preparing for the right moment to make the jump."

‌



Jamie Carragher shares what he has heard about Arne Slot's Liverpool future READ MORE :

OPINION Tom Sunderland Liverpool dream 2026/27 squad as Mo Salah successor arrives and Adam Wharton decision made

The 42-year-old has demonstrated considerable tactical versatility by employing a range of formations during his early years in management, including a fluid 5-3-2 system. This season, Torres has predominantly opted for a 4-2-3-1 shape. Here is how Liverpool's squad could set up under the Reds legend.

Alisson Becker looks set to remain first-choice goalkeeper next season, despite Giorgi Mamardashvili stepping in for the Brazilian on several occasions. The Reds exercised their option to extend the shot-stopper's contract by a further year last month.

‌



At the back, Jeremy Jacquet will head to Anfield having agreed his lucrative transfer from Rennes in the January window. Given his experience of coaching young players, Torres would relish the opportunity to work alongside the gifted 20-year-old. Jacquet's arrival could limit Virgil van Dijk's playing time, potentially leading Ibrahima Konate to pair up with his fellow Frenchman, who is currently negotiating a new deal.

Milos Kerkez is poised to make the left-back berth his own as Andy Robertson prepares to leave this summer. Meanwhile, Jeremie Frimpong will be eager to win the battle for the right-back position as Connor Bradley continues his recovery from injury.

View 2 Images Torres would welcome working with Rio Ngumoha due to his experience as a youth coach (Image: Liverpool FC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Looking at the midfield, Ryan Gravenberch and Alexis Mac Allister haven't quite hit the levels they showed last term, yet the partnership formed the foundation of Liverpool's title-winning side under Slot. Torres would be banking on the pair rediscovering their form while offering support for Florian Wirtz, who would enjoy the freedom to operate as a number 10.

Mohamed Salah is set to say goodbye to the Reds in the summer. Securing a direct replacement for Salah would be near impossible and deploying Dominik Szoboszlai on the right wing would enable one of the squad's most impressive performers to swap positions with Wirtz going forward, while offering protection for Frimpong out wide.

On the left flank, Torres could promote Rio Ngumoha to regular first-team action following his emergence this campaign. Alexander Isak is poised to spearhead Liverpool's attack at the beginning of next season, allowing the ex-Newcastle United striker to demonstrate his quality after Hugo Ekitike's injury setback. However, Torres could revert to his previous 5-3-2 system once both forwards are available.

Sports.title: Arsene Wenger has pinpointed the exact moment he believes Arsenal lost their soul
Sports.content:
Arsene Wenger has pinpointed the exact moment he believes Arsenal lost their soul

The former Arsenal manager has opened up about the moment he believes the club lost its soul

View Image Wenger pinpointed the moment his former club lost their soul (Image: AP)

Arsenal are chasing their first Premier League title in almost 22 years but former manager Arsene Wenger has previously pinpointed what he believes went wrong at the club after their last triumph. The Frenchman argued that the Gunners 'left their soul' behind at Highbury when they moved to the Emirates - despite the new stadium sitting just 500 metres away.

‌



Highbury had been Arsenal's home for 93 years before it was converted into flats, though the iconic art‑deco East Stand facade still remains. It was there that Arsenal won three Premier League titles and regularly challenged at the top, only to stagnate following the move.

‌



Wenger, who managed the club for 22 years, admitted the relocation came at a cost. "I moved from Highbury, which was similar to Anfield, but there was a soul in the stadium," the former manager told beIN Sports back in 2020.

‌

"The inclination of the stands had to be smaller all those things together that we didn't find to recreate the atmosphere."

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho comment that silenced Vincent Kompany is bad news for Arsenal
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho comment that silenced Vincent Kompany is bad news for Arsenal

Arsenal will need to finish the season strongly if they are to claim top spot ahead of Vincent Kompany's former club Manchester City

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta came up short against Pep Guardiola on Sunday (Image: Getty Images)

As Arsenal go into a crucial final month of the season, the biggest obstacle between them and the Premier League title may that their current players have never won it before. Liverpool had several near misses before beating Manchester City to top spot in 2019/20 and - as Jose Mourinho pointed out - they only ended the drought after winning the Champions League.

‌



Most of the current Arsenal squad have not won a trophy - their last piece of silverware was the 2020 FA Cup. If Mourinho is right in that winning silverware is key to clinching the Premier League title then it is worrying news for the Gunners.

‌



Mourinho the pointed comment ahead City vs Liverpool in November 2019. "They (Liverpool) were not the best (in previous seasons), they were there, they were almost there, but you (City) were the best team, in this moment I don't think there is that difference in power," Mourinho told then City defender Vincent Kompany.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

He continued: "Even in terms of statures, if statures play something. You are the champions of England but they are the champions of Europe.

"They know how to win, they know how to cope with the pressure, so for me, the game today is very, very important. Because if the distances are three points or six points, it is still very open, but if the difference is nine points, goodbye."

‌



View 2 Images Jose Mourinho was proved right as Liverpool beat Manchester City to the title (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Former City captain Vincent Kompany had attempted to play down the significance of the clash with it being so early in the season. However, Mourinho felt Liverpool's triumph in Europe was an important factor in Jurgen Klopp's side coming out on top.

‌



Liverpool got the win that day, with early goals from Fabinho and Mohamed Salah paving the way for a 3-1 victory. As predicted by Mourinho, the nine-point gap opened up by that result would prove impossible for City to claw back.

It has been a different story this year, though, with City reeling in Arsenal despite Mikel Arteta's side holding a lead which at times looked unassailable. Victory at Burnley on Wednesday would see the two sides level on points at the top, with City moving ahead on goal difference if they can win by two or more goals.

Arsenal's performance in their defeat at the Etihad Stadium last time out gave some fans optimism. However, Mourinho's warning in 2019 may end up demonstrating why Liverpool were able to end City's dominance in a way which Arsenal cannot.
